mainTopic: The prohibition of גסות הרוח, the fate of the arrogant, and the value of humility
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier teaching: even secret צדקה does not save a certain sinner from גיהנם. The גמרא then asks where the תורה warns against גסות הרוח. It brings פסוקים from ירמיהו and דברים, which count as prohibitions because of רבי אילעא's rule that השמר, פן and אל signal a לא תעשה. Next comes a long series of teachings about the arrogant person: he is made small and disappears unless he does תשובה; he is cut down like an אשירה; he will not rise at תחיית המתים; and ה׳ cannot share the world with him. Against this, the גמרא praises humility: ה׳ comes down to the lowly, as He did at הר סיני and the סנה. רב and רבא say a תלמיד חכם needs a tiny measure of pride, but רב נחמן בר יצחק says he should have none at all. חזקיה, רבי זירא and רבי יוחנן use the words בשר and אדם to teach that the humble person is heard and healed. The amud ends as רב אשי begins a proof that the arrogant person is lowered, and his פסוק comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Even secret צדקה does not save him from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier teaching: even if this sinner gives צדקה in secret, he is not freed from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if he gives charity in secret, as it is written: "A gift in secret calms anger," he will still not be cleared from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a statement that began before this section, about someone who sins with a married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving צדקה in secret is a very great deed; the פסוק even says it calms ה׳'s anger. You might think it would protect him. The teaching says it does not: he still faces the judgment of גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: He will not be cleared or go unpunished
The place of punishment after death

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the last piece of a teaching from just before this section, so do not look for its beginning here.

phrases.english: Even if he gives charity in secret,
as it is written: "A gift in secret calms anger, etc."
phrases.notes: משלי 21:14

phrases.english: he will not be cleared from the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ עוֹשֶׂה צְדָקָה בַּסֵּתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching that began on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even secret צדקה does not save this sinner from the judgment of גיהנם.

steps.title: Where does the Torah warn against arrogance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the אזהרה (Torah warning) against being arrogant.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know there is a warning against arrogant people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks where the Torah actually forbids גסות הרוח, and this sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא spoke about how bad arrogance is. Now it wants more than that: it wants a real prohibition, a לא תעשה, written in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning, meaning a Torah prohibition

phrases.english: From where is the warning for the arrogant?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַזְהָרָה לְגַסֵּי הָרוּחַ מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the source for the prohibition of arrogance
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק serves as the Torah warning against arrogance

steps.title: First source: a פסוק in ירמיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of זעירי brings the פסוק "Hear and listen, do not be haughty."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of זעירי: the source is "Hear and listen, do not be haughty."
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the question. The פסוק plainly says "do not be haughty."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אל ("do not") makes this an instruction against pride. The plain wording of the פסוק already forbids arrogance.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not be haughty, do not raise yourselves up

phrases.english: Rava said that Ze'eiri said:
"Hear and listen, do not be haughty."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 13:15

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר זְעֵירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning comes from ירמיהו: אל תגבהו.

steps.title: Second source: פסוקים in דברים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a different source: pride leads to forgetting ה׳, and the Torah warns us not to forget ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said the source is from here: "Your heart will be lifted up and you will forget," and it is written: "Watch yourself, lest you forget ה׳ your God."
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different source. He joins two פסוקים from the same section in דברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק links a proud heart to forgetting ה׳. The second פסוק warns "watch yourself, lest you forget." Put together, the warning against forgetting also covers the pride that causes it.

keyTerms.meaning: And your heart will be lifted up, meaning pride

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: from here:
"And your heart will be lifted up, and you will forget"
phrases.notes: דברים 8:14

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן תִּשְׁכַּח אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: and it is written: "Watch yourself, lest you forget ה׳ your God."
phrases.notes: דברים 8:11

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning comes from דברים: pride causes forgetting, and "השמר פן תשכח" warns against it.

steps.title: Why these verses count as real prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both sources follow the rule of רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא: the words השמר, פן and אל always mean a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These sources follow what רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעא. For רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעא: wherever it says "watch," "lest," or "do not," it is nothing other than a negative commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוקים just quoted count as true prohibitions and not just good advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי's פסוק uses אל, and רב נחמן בר יצחק's פסוק uses השמר and פן. Because of רבי אילעא's rule, each of these words turns the פסוק into a לא תעשה. So both answers really give an אזהרה against arrogance.

keyTerms.meaning: Every place where it is said
And this is like the view of רבי...

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah warns against גסות הרוח. Both sources work because of the rule that השמר, פן and אל signal a לא תעשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule of רבי אילעא is used across ש״ס to tell when a פסוק is a real prohibition.

phrases.english: And this is like what Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ile'a.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Avin said that Rabbi Ile'a said:
Every place where it says "watch," "lest," or "do not,"
it is nothing other than a negative commandment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִדְרַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rule that makes both sources count as prohibitions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words השמר, פן and אל in a פסוק always mean a לא תעשה.

steps.title: An arrogant person ends up made small
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא, quoting רב אסי or רב אמי, teaches that an arrogant person ends up diminished, based on "רומו מעט."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא taught, sometimes in the name of רב אסי and sometimes in the name of רב אמי: any person who has arrogance will in the end be made small, as it says: "They are raised up for a little while."
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching on arrogance begins. This one is about the result of arrogance, not the prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the proud are "raised up a little," and רב עוירא reads מעט as a hint that they will be made small. Their high position does not last. The גמרא also tells us that רב עוירא sometimes said this in the name of רב אסי and sometimes in the name of רב אמי.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded, taught a lesson from a פסוק
They are raised up for a little while

phrases.english: Rav Avira expounded,

phrases.aramaic: זִמְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַסִּי
phrases.english: sometimes he said it in the name of Rav Asi

phrases.aramaic: וְזִמְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: and sometimes he said it in the name of Rav Ami:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
phrases.english: Any person who has arrogance in him
in the end is made small,
as it says: "They are raised up for a little while."
phrases.notes: איוב 24:24. The word "little" is read as a hint that the proud person ends up little.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב עַוִּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the prohibition of arrogance to its consequence
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An arrogant person will in the end be made small.

steps.title: He does not even remain in the world
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא adds that the arrogant person is not just made small; the next words, "ואיננו," show he will not remain at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in case you say that he is made small but is still alive in the world, the פסוק teaches: "and he is gone."
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוירא heads off a possible mistake: someone might think the arrogant person just loses standing but goes on living. He finishes his teaching from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being "made small" could mean only losing honor. The next word of the פסוק, ואיננו ("and he is not"), shows the punishment goes further: he is gone from the world.

keyTerms.meaning: And in case you will say
He still exists in the world
And he is not, he is gone

steps.whatToRemember: Arrogance is forbidden. The arrogant person ends up made small, and in the end he is gone from the world.

phrases.english: And in case you say he still remains in the world,
the verse teaches: "and he is gone."
phrases.notes: These are the very next words in the same פסוק in איוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר יֶשְׁנוֹ בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב עוירא's teaching and heads off a possible mistake
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The arrogant person does not merely lose standing; he does not remain in the world.

steps.title: If the arrogant person repents, he dies at his proper time like the אבות
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא continues: if the arrogant person does תשובה, he dies at his proper time like אברהם, יצחק and יעקב. If he does not, he is cut off like the top of the grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he repents, he is taken from the world at his proper time, like אברהם אבינו. The פסוק says 'like all (כַּכֹּל) they are gathered in,' and the word 'כל' is used about אברהם, יצחק and יעקב. If he does not repent, 'like the top of the grain they are cut off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the drash on the פסוק in איוב. It shows that there are two possible endings for an arrogant person, depending on whether he does תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier steps the arrogant person was made small and then disappeared. Now we learn that תשובה changes this: he gets a full life and dies with honor, like the אבות. The link to the אבות comes from the word 'כל', which the תורה uses in a ברכה about each of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Repents, takes back his bad way (here, his arrogance)
Is gathered in (dies) at his proper time
Like all. This word links the פסוק to the אבות
An ear (head) of grain on a stalk

phrases.english: But if he repents from it —
phrases.notes: "It" is the arrogance from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: he is gathered in at his proper time, like Avraham our father,
as it says: "They are brought low; like all, they are gathered in."
phrases.notes: איוב 24:24

phrases.english: Like Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov,
about whom it is written: "in all," "of all," "all."
phrases.notes: בראשית 24:1, 27:33, 33:11. Each of the אבות has the word 'כל' in a ברכה.

phrases.english: And if not —
"and like the top of the ear of grain they are cut off."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם חוֹזֵר בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב עוירא's reading of the same פסוק in איוב by adding the תשובה option.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An arrogant person who does תשובה dies at his proper time like the אבות. One who does not is cut off like the top of the grain.

steps.title: What does 'like the top of the grain' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'וּכְרֹאשׁ שִׁבֹּלֶת' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'like the top of the ear of grain' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the meaning of the last phrase of the פסוק. This question sets up the disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not clear which part of the grain the פסוק means by 'ראש'. The answer will decide what picture the פסוק gives of how the arrogant person is cut off.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asks for the meaning of a word or phrase)

phrases.english: What is "and like the top of the ear of grain"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וּכְרֹאשׁ שִׁבֹּלֶת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of a phrase just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the grain 'ראש שבלת' refers to.

steps.title: Two views: the bristly tip, or the ear of grain itself
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One says it means the bristly hairs on top of the grain. The other says it means the ear of grain itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One says: like the bristly tip on top of the grain. The other says: like the ear of grain itself.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view reads 'ראש' simply as the very top part of the grain, the thin bristles. The second view says the פסוק means the whole ear of grain, which leaves the word 'ראש' unexplained. That gap leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The thin bristles sticking up from the top of an ear of grain
One says (when we are not told which אמורא said which view)

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda disagree:
One says: like the bristly tip of the ear of grain,
And one says: like the ear of grain itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the bristly tip of the grain, or the whole ear of grain.

steps.title: Where is the word 'top' in the second view?
steps.stepSummary: The first view fits the word 'ראש' well. The גמרא asks how the second view, 'the ear itself,' explains the word 'ראש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The view that says 'the bristly tip' fits well, because the פסוק says 'the top of the grain.' But according to the view that says 'the ear itself,' why does the פסוק say 'the top of the grain'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second view because it seems to ignore the word 'ראש' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is built with 'בשלמא ... אלא': one view fits the words, and the other seems not to. If the פסוק meant the whole ear of grain, it would not need the word 'ראש'.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one view), before asking a question on the other
That is why it is written
But according to the one who says (opens the question)

phrases.english: It works well for the one who says
like the bristly tip of the ear of grain —
that is why it is written: "like the top of the ear of grain,"
But according to the one who says
like the ear of grain itself,
what is "like the top of the ear of grain"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second opinion from the step before.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that 'ראש שבלת' means the ear of grain itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That view leaves the word 'ראש' in the פסוק without a meaning.

steps.title: The farmer picks the tallest stalks first
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי, and also the school of רבי ישמעאל, explain with a משל: a farmer in his field picks the tallest stalks first. So 'ראש' means the tallest stalks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: It is like a person who goes into his field and picks the tallest stalks first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and saves the second view by explaining 'ראש' a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'ראש' does not mean the top part of one stalk. It means the stalks that stand highest, which are picked first. In the same way, the arrogant person, who 'stands tall,' is cut off first.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: Rav Asi said,
and so too the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
It is like a person who enters his field —
he picks the tallest ones first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי, וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the second view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a new meaning: 'ראש' means the tallest stalks.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ראש' must mean the top part of a stalk.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ראש' means the tallest stalks, which are picked first, so the second view fits the פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: The arrogant person is like the tallest stalk: he stands out, and so he is cut down first.

steps.title: Is the humble person with ה׳, or is ה׳ with the humble person?
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'וְאֶת דַּכָּא וּשְׁפַל רוּחַ', רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One says the humble person is with ה׳. The other says ה׳ is with the humble person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'and with the crushed and lowly of spirit.' רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One says: the crushed one is with Me. The other says: I am with the crushed one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from arrogance to its opposite, humility. Two אמוראים disagree about how to read a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading, ה׳ raises the humble person up to Him. In the second reading, ה׳ comes down to be with the humble person.

phrases.english: "And with the crushed and lowly of spirit."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 57:15

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda disagree:
One says: The crushed one is with Me,
And one says: I am with the crushed one.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְאֶת דַּכָּא וּשְׁפַל רוּחַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of arrogance to the topic of humility.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a disagreement: either the humble person is raised to ה׳, or ה׳ comes down to the humble person.

steps.title: ה׳ comes down to the humble, as at הר סיני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it makes more sense that ה׳ is with the humble person. Proof: ה׳ passed over all the high mountains and rested His שכינה on low הר סיני, and He did not raise הר סיני up to Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes more sense to follow the one who says 'I am with the crushed one.' The Holy One, Blessed be He, passed over all the mountains and hills and rested His שכינה on הר סיני, and He did not lift הר סיני up high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides between the two views from the step before and brings a reason for its choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At הר סיני, ה׳ chose a low mountain and came down to it, instead of lifting it up. This shows that ה׳ comes down to what is low, which supports the reading 'I am with the crushed one.'

keyTerms.meaning: And it makes sense, it stands to reason

phrases.english: And it makes sense like the one who says
I am with the crushed one,
for the Holy One, Blessed be He,
passed over all the mountains and hills,
and rested His Presence on Mount Sinai,
and did not raise Mount Sinai up high.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the disagreement from the step before.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ה׳ comes down to be with the humble person, just as He came down to low הר סיני instead of raising it up.
steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ seeks out what is low: He chose הר סיני and comes down to the humble person.

steps.title: Learn humility from ה׳'s choice of הר סיני and the thornbush
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that a person should copy ה׳'s ways. ה׳ chose low הר סיני over all the mountains, and a thornbush (סנה) over all the beautiful trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A person should always learn from the mind of his Creator. ה׳ passed over all the mountains and hills and rested His שכינה on הר סיני. And He passed over all the beautiful trees and rested His שכינה in the thornbush.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף builds on the last step about הר סיני and turns it into a life lesson: be humble, like ה׳ shows us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 used הר סיני to prove that ה׳ is with the humble. רב יוסף adds a second example, the סנה, and makes it practical: we should learn from what ה׳ chooses. Both examples show ה׳ choosing the lowly over the impressive.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A person should always learn from the mind of his Creator,
for behold, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
passed over all the mountains and hills,
and rested His Divine Presence on Mount Sinai.
And He passed over all the beautiful trees,
and rested His Divine Presence in the thornbush.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לְעוֹלָם יִלְמַד אָדָם מִדַּעַת קוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the הר סיני proof from step 14 and turns it into a lesson for how people should act.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should learn humility from ה׳, who chose the lowly הר סיני and the lowly סנה.

steps.title: An arrogant person deserves to be cut down like an אשירה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says an arrogant person deserves to be cut down like a tree used for עבודה זרה. He proves it from the shared word גדע, 'cut down', in two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Any person who has arrogance in him deserves to be cut down like an אשירה. It says here (about proud people): 'And the tall ones will be cut down,' and it says there: 'And their אשירות you shall cut down.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר begins a series of statements about how bad arrogance is. This first one compares the arrogant person to an idolatrous tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same root, גדע (cut down), appears in a פסוק about tall, proud people and in a פסוק about אשירות. Because the word is shared, רבי אלעזר links them: the proud person is treated like the idolatrous tree.

keyTerms.meaning: a tree worshipped as עבודה זרה
it is written here... and it is written there (linking two פסוקים by a shared word)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
phrases.english: Any person who has arrogance in him
deserves to be cut down like an asheira.
It is written here: "And the tall of stature will be cut down,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 10:33. 'Here' means the פסוק about proud, tall people.

phrases.english: and it is written there: "And their asheirot you shall cut down."
phrases.notes: דברים 7:5.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from praising humility to condemning its opposite, arrogance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An arrogant person deserves to be cut down like an אשירה, learned from the shared word גדע.

steps.title: An arrogant person's dust will not wake up at תחיית המתים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says an arrogant person will not rise at תחיית המתים. He reads the פסוק's word 'dwellers of the dust' as people who lived close to the dust, meaning humbly, during their lives.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Any person who has arrogance in him, his dust will not be stirred up. As it says: 'Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust.' It does not say 'you who lie in the dust,' but 'you who dwell in the dust.' This means someone who made himself a neighbor to the dust during his life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second statement about arrogance. He reads one word of a פסוק very closely to show that only humble people will be woken at תחיית המתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said שכבי, 'those who lie' in the dust, which would include all dead people. Instead it says שכני, 'those who dwell' or 'neighbors' of the dust. רבי אלעזר learns from this that it means people who were humble, 'close to the ground', while alive.

keyTerms.meaning: his dust (his remains in the grave)
those who dwell in (are neighbors of) the dust
those who lie in the dust
it does not say ..., but rather ... (reading the exact word choice)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof rests on one letter: שֹׁכְנֵי (dwell) versus שֹׁכְבֵי (lie). Read those two words slowly so you see the difference.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ —
phrases.english: Any person who has arrogance in him,
his dust will not be stirred up,
phrases.notes: He means this person will not be brought back to life at תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: as it is said: "Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 26:19.

phrases.english: "those who lie in the dust" is not said,
but rather "those who dwell in the dust":
one who made himself a neighbor to the dust in his lifetime.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ — אֵין עֲפָרוֹ נִנְעָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement by the same רבי אלעזר about the arrogant person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one who was humble in life, a 'neighbor to the dust', will be stirred up at תחיית המתים.

steps.title: The שכינה wails over an arrogant person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר's third statement: the שכינה cries over an arrogant person, based on the פסוק about how ה׳ relates to the haughty 'from afar'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Any person who has arrogance in him, the שכינה wails over him. As it says: 'And the haughty one, from afar He knows.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר finishes his series with a third statement: ה׳ is pained and cries over the arrogant person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק contrasts how ה׳ treats the lowly with how He treats the haughty, whom He knows only 'from afar'. רבי אלעזר reads this as ה׳ being distant from the arrogant person and wailing over him. This ties back to step 14: ה׳ is close to the humble and far from the proud.
steps.whatToRemember: This section is all about humility. ה׳ rests on the low (הר סיני, the סנה), so we should learn to be humble. The arrogant person is cut down like an אשירה, does not rise at תחיית המתים, and makes the שכינה cry.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ,
phrases.english: Any person who has arrogance in him,
the Divine Presence wails over him,
as it is said: "And the haughty one, from afar He knows."
phrases.notes: תהלים 138:6. The start of this פסוק says ה׳ cares for the lowly; this part is about the haughty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ, שְׁכִינָה מְיַלֶּלֶת עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third statement in רבי אלעזר's series on arrogance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה wails over an arrogant person, based on 'וגבה ממרחק יידע'.

steps.title: ה׳ is high, yet He sees the lowly
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא (or רבי אלעזר) contrasts people with ה׳. A high person pays attention only to other high people. ה׳ is the highest of all, yet He looks at the lowly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא taught, and some say it was רבי אלעזר: Come and see how ה׳'s way is different from a human's way. Among people, an important person notices other important people but does not notice a lowly person. ה׳ is not like that. He is high, and He sees the lowly, as the פסוק says: 'For ה׳ is high, and He sees the lowly.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that contrasts how people treat the lowly with how ה׳ treats them. It is proven from a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the earlier idea that ה׳ rests His שכינה with the humble. People with status tend to ignore those below them. The פסוק shows that ה׳'s greatness does not stop Him from looking at the lowly, and in fact He looks at them specifically.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)
The way of flesh and blood, meaning how people behave

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ רַב עַוִּירָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rav Avira taught, and some say it was Rabbi Elazar:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.
The way of flesh and blood:
the high one sees the high one,
but the high one does not see the lowly.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ כֵּן,
phrases.english: But the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so:
He is high, and He sees the lowly,
as it says: 'For ה׳ is high, and He sees the lowly.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 138:6

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב עַוִּירָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching to the collection about humility and arrogance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike people, ה׳ is high and still pays attention to the lowly.

steps.title: ה׳ cannot share the world with an arrogant person
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא (or מר עוקבא) says ה׳ declares that He and an arrogant person cannot live in the world together. He reads the פסוק's 'אֹתוֹ' (him) as 'אִתּוֹ' (with him).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said, and some say it was מר עוקבא: About anyone who has arrogance, ה׳ says, 'He and I cannot live together in the world.' The פסוק says: 'One who slanders his friend in secret, him I will destroy; one with haughty eyes and a proud heart, him I cannot bear.' Do not read it as 'אֹתוֹ' (him). Read it as 'אִתּוֹ לֹא אוּכָל', 'with him I cannot be.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a strong statement: ה׳ refuses to share the world with an arrogant person. It reads one word of a פסוק a little differently to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple פסוק says ה׳ cannot bear the arrogant person. The אל תקרי reading changes 'him' to 'with him', so the point becomes that ה׳ cannot live alongside him. Arrogance pushes the שכינה away.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as... (a reading that changes the vowels of a word)
Haughty of eyes, looking down on others

steps.confusionAlert: אַל תִּקְרֵי does not mean the פסוק is spelled wrong. The letters stay the same; the גמרא reads them with different vowels to learn an extra lesson.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said, and some say it was Mar Ukva:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ,
phrases.english: Any person who has arrogance in him,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אֲנִי וָהוּא יְכוֹלִין לָדוּר בָּעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: I and he cannot live together in the world,
as it says: 'One who slanders his friend in secret, him I will destroy;
phrases.notes: תהלים 101:5

phrases.aramaic: גְּבַהּ עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב לֵבָב אֹתוֹ לֹא אוּכָל״.
phrases.english: one with haughty eyes and a proud heart, him I cannot bear.'
Do not read it as 'him',
but rather 'with him I cannot be.'
phrases.notes: Same letters, different vowels: ה׳ is saying He cannot live together with such a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ה׳'s closeness to the humble to His distance from the arrogant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ says He and an arrogant person cannot live in the world together.

steps.title: Another version: it is about people who speak לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: Some teach that רב חסדא's statement, 'I and he cannot live together', was said about people who speak לשון הרע, based on the first half of the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this statement about people who speak לשון הרע, as the פסוק says: 'One who slanders his friend in secret, him I will destroy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the previous teaching. In this version, the people ה׳ cannot live with are those who speak לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק has two halves: the slanderer and the haughty person. The first version tied the teaching to the second half, about arrogance. This version ties it to the first half, about secret slander.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (another version)
People who speak negatively about others

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַמְּסַפְּרֵי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע,
phrases.english: There are those who teach it about people who speak לשון הרע,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the statement just taught: 'I and he cannot live together in the world.'

phrases.english: as it says: 'One who slanders his friend in secret, him I will destroy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַמְּסַפְּרֵי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of whom step 20's statement is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, ה׳ cannot live in the world with people who speak לשון הרע.

steps.title: Even a slight wind shakes an arrogant person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי says an arrogant person is upset by even a small wind. He compares the wicked to the stormy sea and uses a קל וחומר: if a huge sea is stirred by a little wind, a small person surely is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי said: Anyone who has arrogance in him is stirred up by even a slight wind, as the פסוק says: 'The wicked are like the stormy sea.' If the sea, which holds many רביעיות of water, is stirred up by a slight wind, then a person, who has only one רביעית of lifeblood, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching about arrogance: an arrogant person is unsettled by the smallest thing. It uses a פסוק and a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the wicked to a restless sea. If something as huge as the sea is churned up by a light breeze, a person who holds only one רביעית of essential blood is surely shaken. The arrogant person lacks calm and is upset by small things.

keyTerms.meaning: A slight wind, a little breeze
A quarter of a לוג, a small measure of liquid
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ,
phrases.english: Any person who has arrogance in him,
even a slight wind stirs him up,
as it says: 'The wicked are like the stormy sea.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 57:20

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה יָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כַּמָּה רְבִיעִיּוֹת —
phrases.english: Now, if the sea, which has so many רביעיות in it,
is stirred up by a slight wind,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אֶלָּא רְבִיעִית אַחַת —
phrases.english: a person, who has only one רביעית in him,
phrases.notes: He means the one רביעית of blood a person needs to stay alive.

phrases.english: all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another consequence of arrogance, built on a קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An arrogant person is easily shaken, since even a slight wind stirs the huge sea.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם needs a tiny bit of pride
steps.stepSummary: After all the warnings against arrogance, רב teaches a balance: a תלמיד חכם should have a very small amount of pride, one eighth of an eighth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: A תלמיד חכם needs to have one part of eight in an eighth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the discussion around. Even though arrogance is very bad, רב says a תלמיד חכם should have a tiny measure of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, every teaching attacked arrogance. רב adds that a Torah scholar needs a very small amount of self-respect, measured as one eighth of an eighth. The point is a careful balance, not permission to be proud.

keyTerms.meaning: One part of eight in an eighth, a tiny amount

steps.confusionAlert: This is not praise for arrogance. The measure is tiny on purpose; the earlier teachings against גסות הרוח still stand.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:
A Torah scholar needs to have in him
one part of eight in an eighth.
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't say it, but this means one eighth of an eighth of pride.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the teachings against arrogance: a scholar needs a tiny measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם should have one eighth of an eighth of pride.

steps.title: That small pride is like a crown
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע adds that this small measure of pride crowns the scholar, like the thin bristle on top of a stalk of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: And it crowns him like the bristle on top of the grain stalk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a picture to explain רב's tiny measure of pride. It is compared to the small bristle at the tip of a grain stalk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bristle on a stalk of grain is thin and small, but it sits on top like a crown. A scholar's small pride should also be tiny, yet it gives him a fitting dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: The thin bristle at the tip of a grain

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
And it crowns him like the bristle on the grain stalk.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the eighth of an eighth of pride from רב's teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and adds a picture to רב's measure in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scholar's tiny pride crowns him like the bristle on top of a grain stalk.

steps.title: רבא: too much pride or none at all is wrong
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a scholar who has pride deserves שמתא, and one who has none deserves שמתא too. The right amount is only the tiny measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: In שמתא if he has it, and in שמתא if he does not have it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a sharp warning on both sides. A scholar who has real arrogance deserves שמתא, and so does one with no pride at all. The next step brings רב נחמן בר יצחק, who disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets both limits on רב's teaching. Full arrogance is forbidden, but having zero pride is also wrong for a תלמיד חכם. Only the tiny 'eighth of an eighth' is the right path.

keyTerms.meaning: That he does not have it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע and רבא, a תלמיד חכם needs a tiny, crown-like measure of pride: not more, and not none. The next step brings רב נחמן בר יצחק, who disagrees.

phrases.english: Rava said:
In excommunication is the one who has it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means arrogance: a scholar who has real arrogance deserves a ban.

phrases.english: and in excommunication is the one who does not have it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּשַׁמְתָּא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets limits on both sides of רב's tiny measure of pride.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar with arrogance deserves שמתא, and so does one with no pride at all.

steps.title: No pride at all, not even a tiny bit
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says a תלמיד חכם should have no pride at all, not even the tiny measure, because the פסוק calls every proud person an abomination.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Not any of it, and not even part of it. Is it a small thing that it is written about it: "Everyone proud of heart is an abomination to ה׳"?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק disagrees with רב and רבא from the earlier steps. He says a scholar should not have even the tiny "one eighth of an eighth" of pride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps allowed a very small measure of pride for a scholar. רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects even that small amount. His proof is that the פסוק says "כל גבה לב", every proud person, with no exception for a little pride or for scholars.

keyTerms.meaning: Not any of it and not even part of it
Is it a small thing? (a way of saying: this is very serious)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב נחמן בר יצחק is just repeating רבא. רבא said a scholar with no pride at all deserves שמתא, while רב נחמן בר יצחק says a scholar should have no pride at all. They disagree.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Not any of it, and not even part of it,
phrases.notes: "It" means pride. Even the tiny "one eighth of an eighth" from earlier is not allowed.

phrases.english: Is it a small thing that it is written about it:
"Everyone proud of heart is an abomination to ה׳"?
phrases.notes: משלי 16:5

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לָא מִינַּהּ וְלָא מִקְצָתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the tiny measure of pride allowed by רב, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם should have no pride at all, since the פסוק condemns every proud person.

steps.title: Prayer is heard only from a humble heart
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה teaches that a person's prayer is heard only if he makes his heart like lowly flesh, based on the פסוק "all flesh will come to bow down."
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: A person's prayer is heard only if he makes his heart like flesh, as it says: "And it will be, from one new month to the next, all flesh will come to bow down."
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה adds a new teaching about humility: only a humble person's prayer is heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about coming to bow before ה׳ calls the people "בשר", flesh. חזקיה reads this as a hint that the one who comes to pray successfully is the one who sees himself as simple flesh, without arrogance.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes his heart like flesh, sees himself as lowly

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:
A person's prayer is not heard

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מֵשִׂים לִבּוֹ כְּבָשָׂר,
phrases.english: unless he makes his heart like flesh,
as it is said: "And it will be, from one new month to the next, etc.
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 66:23

phrases.english: all flesh will come to bow down, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: אֵין תְּפִלָּתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם נִשְׁמַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of avoiding arrogance, showing a reward for humility.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prayer is heard only from someone who sees himself as lowly flesh.

steps.title: "Flesh" is healed, "person" is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא points out that in the צרעת section, the פסוק about "flesh" mentions healing, but the פסוקים about "a person" do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: About "flesh" it is written "and it is healed"; about "a person" it is not written "and it is healed."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives another hint from the word בשר: the one called "flesh" gets healed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the צרעת פסוקים, the case called "בשר" says "ונרפא" (it is healed), while the cases called "אדם" do not. The lesson is that one who sees himself as mere flesh is healed, but one who thinks highly of himself as a great "אדם" is not.

keyTerms.meaning: A person, here hinting at someone who thinks of himself as important

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
About "flesh" it is written "and it is healed,"
phrases.notes: This is about צרעת: ויקרא 13:18.

phrases.english: about "a person" it is not written "and it is healed."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:2 and 13:9 talk about "אדם" and never say healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: ״בָּשָׂר״ כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ ״וְנִרְפָּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on חזקיה's use of "בשר" as a sign of humility, adding healing as another reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sees himself as lowly flesh is healed; one who sees himself as important is not.

steps.title: The letters of "אדם" and "בשר" show how lowly a person is
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the letters of אדם and בשר as hints to lowly things: dust, blood, bile; and shame, rot, worm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: אדם stands for אפר (dust), דם (blood), מרה (bile). בשר stands for בושה (shame), סרוחה (rotten), רמה (worm).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן uses the letters of the words אדם and בשר to show how small and lowly a human really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter of the word starts another word. א-ד-ם gives אפר, דם, מרה, and ב-ש-ר gives בושה, סרוחה, רמה. Thinking about this should break a person's arrogance.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: אדם (person):
dust, blood, bile.
phrases.notes: Each word starts with one letter of אדם, in order.

phrases.english: בשר (flesh): shame, rotten, worm.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אָדָם: אֵפֶר, דָּם, מָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why אדם and בשר are words of lowliness, supporting the humility teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The letters of אדם and בשר hint at how lowly a human being is.

steps.title: Another version: the ש stands for שאול
steps.stepSummary: Some say the middle letter of בשר stands for שאול (the grave) instead of סרוחה, because the letter is written as a ש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: שאול, because it is written with a ש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רבי יוחנן's hint for the middle letter of בשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter in בשר sounds like a ס, which fits סרוחה, but it is written like a ש, which fits שאול. This version follows how the letter looks, not how it sounds.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say, there is another version

steps.whatToRemember: The humble person who sees himself as lowly "flesh" is the one whose prayers are heard and who is healed, and the very letters of אדם and בשר remind us how small a human is.

phrases.english: Some say: שאול (the grave),
since it is written with a ש.
phrases.notes: The letter in בשר sounds like ס but looks like ש, so it can stand for שאול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: שְׁאוֹל, דִּכְתִיב בְּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading for the middle letter in רבי יוחנן's hint.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ש of בשר stands for שאול, following how the letter is written.

steps.title: An arrogant person will end up made smaller
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי teaches that anyone who has גסות הרוח will in the end be made smaller, and he starts to bring a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Any person who has arrogance in him will in the end be made smaller, as the פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new teaching: a proud person will end up made smaller. He is setting up a proof from a פסוק, which comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps showed how much the תורה dislikes pride. רב אשי adds what happens to the proud person: his pride backfires, and he ends up lowered instead of raised. The word שנאמר tells us his source, a פסוק, is about to be quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said; introduces a פסוק as proof

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the proof in this line. The line ends with 'as it is said:' and the actual פסוק comes right after it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
phrases.english: Any person who has arrogance in him
will in the end be made smaller,
as it is said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אשי כל אדם שיש בו גסות הרוח לסוף נפחת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings about pride and humility, now describing the downfall that pride brings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with גסות הרוח will eventually be lowered, and this is supported by a פסוק that is about to be quoted.
